Place the decision gateway after that task, not directly after the preceding step, so that the stated activity appears in the model and the branches are driven by the condition each item states.

When the description says a person chooses an option, decides, collects information, or prepares documents, and it names no software, application, form, or system that the person uses for that step: Model such a step as a bpmn:manualTask, because it is human work performed without an execution application. Reserve bpmn:userTask for steps the description ties to a software system, such as a form or application the person works in.

When the description states a performed work action at the very beginning or the very end of the process (for example, an identification step that opens the process, or one of several approval or rejection actions that closes it), and that action is described as something done rather than as a message or condition: Model each such described action as a task, placed after the start event or before the end event. Use the start event only to mark the trigger and each end event only to mark an outcome, and do not put the action's label on the event itself. When the process has several outcomes, give each outcome its own task and end event, following the stated branching.

When the description says that after an awaited item is received (an event on a branch), the process performs one or more further named actions in sequence before a closing action: Model each described action that follows the receipt event as its own task, placed in the stated order between the receipt event and the closing task, connected by sequence flows. Do not drop such an action or merge it into the closing task or the event label.
